Twenty-two comments

La Cardeuse

This is a tune I picked up from the first Patrick Street CD, which was a brilliant CD even the songs were good. I think it is French Canadian, and was played by Jacki Daly on the CD.

↳ Posted by JACKB on February 3rd, 2007.

“La Cardeuse et le Grand Triomphe”

“The Fiddler’s Companion” ~ Andrew Kuntz
http://www.ibiblio.org/fiddlers/CAR_CASU.htm

“A cardeuse refers to the person who performs the task of carding wool, straightening it between wire brushes in preparation for spinning. La Cardeuse is supposedly a dance from the St. Jean region of France, brought to the New World by French immigrants to Québec. The step-dance La Cardeuse is from the Saguenay region of Quebéc, and imitates the carding of wool, according to Hart & Sandell, giving rise to the title. Guy Bouchard notes that, while this ‘crooked’ tune was quite popular in the past, modern fiddlers seem to have forgotten it.”

Trente sous Zero

If you are interested in crooked tunes from Quebec, try this link.

http://www.trentesouszero.com/

This company makes available the dots and music for learning these wonderfully Unique tunes from Quebec. La Cardeuse is in volume II of:

“Airs Tordus, Crooked Tunes, Airs de Violon du Quebec Fiddle Tunes.” The two books are very small/thin and there is a companion CD available as well.

La cardeuse

The version of this tune played by Louis Boudreault and transcribed by Lisa Ornstein in her master’s thesis (and reprinted in 25 Crooked Tunes Vol 2) is very different than this version, even skipping the first two parts given here.

Boudreault’s A part is 5.5 bars long and starts B2d2 d2ef | g2d2 fdef; I don’t think it corresponds well to any of the parts here. His B part is basically the same as the fourth part given here. His C part starts G2AD B2BB | AGAB Bc3 and is similar to the last part here, but it is 8.5 bars long with an additional one bar tag at the end of the second time through. (Also, while Ornstein doesn’t transcribe this, I would swear Boudreault plays the tune AABBBCCC.)

La Cardeuse, X:4

As others have stated, the first two parts make up a single tune, La Cardeuse. But I see its rhythmic structure differently. For me, the first part is in four beats per bar, second part is in five(!) beats per bar. For me that’s the “crookedness” people refer to. The first part doesn’t seem to me to be so crooked.

This setting shows how well it works, and how simple the tune is, when you parse it this way.

Re: La Cardeuse

I completely changed my setting (X:4) for reasons described below.

This setting (X:4) is now based on Pascal Gemme’s playing of the tune La Cardeuse on the album Pascal Gemme & Mario Loiselle - Musique du Monde (2013).
https://music.youtube.com/watch?v=EBntg4Zorb0

To write this transcription, I started with a version by Andrew Kuntz on tunearch.org (https://tunearch.org/wiki/Cardeuse_(La)) and made quite a lot of changes. I’ve submitted my transcription to that site too but it’s been pending validation for months – and I think it could be good to put this transcription here too. It may help a bit.

It’s striking how “crooked” or irregular this setting is – it doesn’t stay in 4/4. And there are a lot of notes – for better or for worse this transcription includes a lot (but by no means all) of the ornamentation and variations played by P Gemme. Still, when you listen to it, it feels perfectly natural – and lively and interesting!

There’s a comment from Sol Foster, 11 years ago, above, about a version played by Louis Boudreault. I haven’t listened to that yet, but just going from the S Foster’s comment, I think Gemme’s version and Boudreault’s are probably quite similar.

My earlier remarks above, about the setting X:4, are now better off being ignored. They were referring to the tune Cotillon De Baie-Ste-Catherine (the first two parts of the Patrick Street set called La Cardeuse) which I feel deserves a separate entry here. So I have made one: https://thesession.org/tunes/23211 .
The setting I was talking about above is now to be found in this separate entry, tune #23211.

↳ Posted by GoPlayer on June 2nd, 2023.
